BUILDING CONSTRUCTION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: BUILDING CONSTRUCTION
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Sanitary Appliances, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Sanitary Appliances.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Sanitary Appliances.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Sanitary Appliances.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Sanitary Appliances.

2. When learning Domestic Water Supply, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Domestic Water Supply.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Domestic Water Supply.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Domestic Water Supply.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Domestic Water Supply.

3. When learning Scaffolding, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Scaffolding.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Scaffolding.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Scaffolding.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Scaffolding.

4. When learning Computer Aided Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Aided Drawing.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Aided Drawing.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Computer Aided Drawing.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Aided Drawing.

5. When learning Windows, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Windows.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Windows.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Windows.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Windows.

6. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Remove all guards
   D. Run with the tool

7. When learning Construction Plant, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Construction Plant.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Construction Plant.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Construction Plant.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Construction Plant.

8. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Input Cable Tester

9. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Monitor
   B. CPU
   C. Speaker
   D. Keyboard

10. When learning Appropriate Technology in Building, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Appropriate Technology in Building.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Appropriate Technology in Building.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Appropriate Technology in Building.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Appropriate Technology in Building.

11. When learning Roof Construction, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Roof Construction.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Roof Construction.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Roof Construction.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Roof Construction.

12. When learning Doors, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Doors.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Doors.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Doors.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Doors.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Site Organisation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Appropriate Technology in Building and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Orthographic Projection and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Aided Drawing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Sanitary Appliances.

2. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Domestic Water Supply.

3. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Scaffolding.

4. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Aided Drawing.

5. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Windows.

6. A — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

7. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Construction Plant.

8. A — Information and Communication Technology

9. B — CPU

10. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Appropriate Technology in Building.

11. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Roof Construction.

12. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Doors.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Site Organisation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Appropriate Technology in Building; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Orthographic Projection; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Computer Aided Drawing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
